As part of leading a Stoic life, I have found it immensely helpful to keep a diary of sorts and reflect back on it.

At the end of each day, I recall each thing that caused me to become emotional. Whether they were obstacles I could not surpass, or the feelings of others that affected my own.

Often, when we are confronted with hardships we allow ourselves to become emotional. Because of this, we cannot analyze problems properly and thus cannot deal with them in the best possible way or, in some cases, move on.

By keeping a journal, we can look back and reflect in a calm state of mind. If someone is angry at you, it is normal to become angry (or sad) as a response. It is almost reflexive behaviour. If someone is angry at you, write it down at the end of your day in your journal. The next morning, after getting a good nights sleep, read your journal. Think back: Why were they angry? Why did this make you angry? In a calmer state of mind, you are more prepared to deal with difficulties like this.

I encourage everyone to take up this practice.
Keep a journal, and reflect often.
